newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: British, Irish PMs to meet in London on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: British, Irish PMs to meet in London on Thursday.

text.p: Ireland's newly elected prime minister, Bertie Ahern, will discuss Northern Ireland with his British counterpart, Tony Blair, in London next Thursday.

The meeting will be the first between Ahern and Blair and will take place against against a background of mounting tension in Northern Ireland as the start of the annual season of Protestant parades and marches next weekend approaches.
It was agreed in a lengthy telephone conversation the two men had on Friday afternoon, Irish officials said.
Britain is sponsoring talks to try to prevent confrontation between Protestants and the minority Roman Catholic community in the British province.
Britain and Ireland are sponsors of a fragile Northern Ireland peace process and hold regular meetings to discuss the outlook for security and political progress.

Ahern, who became head of a minority government on Thursday after an inconclusive general election on June 6, said the same day that the Northern Ireland conflict, in which 3,200 people have died since 1969, was his top political priority.
The two governments want pro-British Unionists and Irish nationalists to work out a lasting settlement.

They are united in shunning contact with Sinn Fein, which is banned from the talks because of the failuire of its Irish Republican Army (IRA) allies to call an end to its war against British rule of the province.
